title: Sole-owner simulation host and control protocol
description: Extract core side effects; build pure HostCore plus native lifecycle, formal command status/revisions, snapshots, event journal, control migration, and bounded storage.

title: Characterize and specify command semantics
description: Freeze executable evidence and the target semantics for every playback, configuration, selection, shutdown, and overload path before changing runtime ownership. Correct the stale audit claim: the current TerminalApp single-step path calls advance_simulation with single_step=true and does not enqueue a second step, so live and headless TUI must be recorded as a one-step green control. Add focused red reproductions for the actual failures: two GPUI SimulationView instances can independently step one world and leave playback commands stuck in the inner WorldState queue; Bevy local control plus later command draining can make a request advance one or two ticks; mixed ControlCommand classes take immediate versus deferred paths and can violate enqueue order; optimistic frontend state can diverge when the capacity-32 queue rejects; and shutdown can strand pending commands without terminal status.
design: Characterization and specification only; do not replace the runtime in this bead. Specify one bounded CommandEnvelope stream ordered by host-assigned AdmissionSequence. No command-class subqueue, reorder, drop, or coalescing is allowed unless the protocol names and tests an equivalence rule. At each boundary, apply admitted envelopes strictly in sequence. Step atomically pauses, performs exactly one pure scientific transition at its position in the order, and remains paused unless a later envelope changes playback; an explicit Step also suppresses an implicit cadence tick in that same boundary. With manual time frozen, Step then Resume means one tick and final Running, while Resume then Step means one tick and final Paused. Rejected and failed envelopes still receive queryable terminal application status; admission, application, journal commit, and crash durability remain distinct.
acceptance_criteria: Executable characterization proves the current TUI live and headless single-step each advance exactly once and removes the false TUI double-step expectation. Focused tests fail for GPUI two-view stepping and stuck playback commands, Bevy one-or-two-step behavior, mixed-class reordering, optimistic queue-full divergence, and shutdown with pending work. A checked target truth table covers Pause, Resume, Speed, Step, config, selection, auto-pause, duplicate CommandId, expected-revision conflict, disconnected clients, queue sizes 1/32/33/1000, and shutdown. It explicitly asserts Step-then-Resume and Resume-then-Step results, when ControlRevision changes, when a science tick may run, and which application and journal status each case returns.
notes: Source evidence at the 2b1c874 baseline: terminal/mod.rs applies drained playback commands and step_once calls advance_simulation directly; render/src/lib.rs gives each SimulationView its own accumulator and steps after only the outer command drain; bevy/src/lib.rs mirrors playback into local state and separately drains WorldState simulation commands; command.rs drops on bounded queue full; control.rs returns a projected config before the queued update is applied. This bead records facts and target policy, not implementation.

title: Make FrankenSQLite persistence bounded, fail-closed, and cancel-clean
description: Extend the existing thread-owned FrankenSQLite worker into the production bounded journal adapter for HostCore. Admission from the host is nonblocking; on queue-full or disconnected rejection the host retains the exact completed batch, latches a visible fault, and advances no later scientific tick until explicit retry. The worker alone creates, uses, closes, and drops fsqlite::Connection and returns typed per-batch, flush, and shutdown acknowledgements.
design: Model and test fault points at admission, worker receive, begin, each statement/table, commit, rollback, post-commit/pre-ack, analytics publication, flush/checkpoint, shutdown, and reopen. Maintain explicit batch/event-sequence watermarks for admitted, applied-to-journal, committed-volatile, and durable progress; never infer one from queue success. ApplicationState remains owned by HostCore and is not rewritten by storage. JournalState becomes CommittedVolatile for memory mode and can never become Durable. File mode may emit Durable only for the exact proven transaction/watermark semantics. Implement a durable outbox/per-batch applied-durable watermark if needed; otherwise document the precise crash-loss window, keep affected statuses Pending or non-durable, and make every API/UI claim reflect that limitation.
acceptance_criteria: Capacity and slow/failing-worker tests prove bounded memory, nonblocking admission, exact retained-batch retry, pause-before-loss, and fail-closed timeout. Fault injection at every defined boundary yields a deterministic status and leaves no active transaction or silently lost lifecycle/command event. Memory-mode flush/shutdown receipts are CommittedVolatile and never Durable. For every file-mode status reported Durable, close/crash-boundary simulation plus independent reopen finds exactly the acknowledged commands/events through the durable watermark and passes integrity/order checks. A post-commit/pre-ack test proves idempotent recovery without duplicate effects, or the implementation withholds Durable and records the exact remaining crash-loss limitation. Shutdown is cancel-clean and reports flush failure/timeout rather than logging success.
notes: This bead builds on the current bounded StoragePipeline and .8.9.4 worker ownership work; it does not move a Connection across threads or add another database engine. Durable outbox and per-batch watermarks are requirements to prove, not assumptions that may be inferred from current enqueue, flush, or analytics behavior.

title: Run runtime lifecycle, contention, and soak matrix
description: Run the final runtime-only lifecycle, contention, and soak matrix against HostCore, the native driver, HostClient, snapshot subscribers, event cursors, and fault-injected storage adapters. Use synthetic clients/subscribers and deterministic fake or real FrankenSQLite journal faults; do not make this bead depend on a live GPUI, Bevy, FrankenTUI, window system, GPU, or renderer reconnect.
design: This is a validation bead after .4.9, not a catch-all implementation lane. Reuse the .4.1 command truth table and .4.5 manual-time traces, then stress the same schedules through the native driver. Separate deterministic correctness runs from wall-clock/resource soaks. Subscriber disconnect/reconnect means synthetic HostClient snapshot/event cursors only. Any renderer presentation, input, device-loss, or window lifecycle failure belongs to .6.x/.7.x live frontend E2E beads and is reported there rather than fixed here.
acceptance_criteria: The matrix covers mixed-class storms at 1/32/33/1000+ commands, duplicate/retry conflicts, Step-then-Resume and Resume-then-Step, simultaneous clients, paused idle, bounded catch-up, stalled/dropped snapshot subscribers, event Gap and journal catch-up, every .4.10 admission/transaction/ack/flush/shutdown fault, cancellation races, shutdown with pending work, and a recorded fixed-seed long-run soak. Manual and native lanes have identical command/application/event/digest traces where required. No deadlock, duplicate step, unbounded queue/memory growth, lost required event, nonterminal admitted command, task leak, or presentation-load-dependent scientific digest is allowed; CPU, memory, queue high-water, p50/p95/p99 latency, soak duration, and exact machine/command are saved.
notes: Runtime synthetic reconnect coverage is intentional. Actual renderer reconnect, two-window behavior after migration, terminal restoration, GPU device failure, screenshots, and visual soak are excluded and remain owned by the presentation E2E beads. Findings here may open focused runtime defects but unrelated fixes do not land in this validation bead.

title: Extract command and storage side effects from core step
description: After the command-semantics characterization, turn one core science transition into a pure explicit operation. Remove simulation-command queue ownership and synchronous WorldPersistence calls from WorldState::step. Accept validated boundary inputs and return a deterministic StepOutcome carrying the current summary, domain and lifecycle records, dirty/revision signals, digest inputs, and persistence projection data needed by the host. A completed scientific transition must not await I/O, depend on a renderer, or change because a later storage admission fails.
design: Land as a reviewed integration series rather than one giant rewrite: characterize all side effects; introduce StepOutcome alongside the old call path; move command application to explicit boundary inputs; move persistence projection/admission after the transition; then retire the internal queues through normal source edits only. Keep StepOutcome compact and renderer/storage-engine neutral: it must not clone a full RenderSnapshot or expose FrankenSQLite types. Gate every slice against the fixed WorldDigestV1 trace and corrected lifecycle-accounting fixtures. This is a semantic boundary extraction, not a mechanical module split or the HostCore implementation.
acceptance_criteria: WorldState owns no transport queue and one pure step performs no filesystem, database, channel, clock, or renderer I/O. Fixed inputs produce the same V1 state/stage digests, summaries, births, deaths, combat records, and resource accounting before and after each integration slice. A fault injected after StepOutcome returns cannot alter or roll back the completed scientific state. Tests cover empty and nonempty outcomes, multiple events between persistence intervals, a rejected downstream batch, serial/parallel supported lanes, and the applicable feature matrix. StepOutcome contains enough information for .4.5 host publication and .4.10 journaling without rereading mutable world state.
notes: Depends on .4.1 so the extraction cannot accidentally preserve the current renderer-specific order as the target contract. Existing .2.5, .2.8, and .3.9 prerequisites remain authoritative. Non-goals: final scheduling, channel selection, snapshot projection, storage durability, visual frontend migration, and physical file/module extraction.

title: Spike Asupersync channels, blocking bridge, and cancellation
description: Decide the enforceable runtime dependency direction and whether a new scriptbots-runtime crate is justified, then run a bounded Asupersync channel/cancellation/blocking-boundary spike against the protocol needs from .4.1. The intended graph is scriptbots-core <- scriptbots-runtime <- scriptbots-storage/application/frontends/control adapters, where each arrow means the component on the right depends on the component on the left. Runtime may depend on core and small selected scheduling primitives; it must not depend on FrankenSQLite, Axum/Tokio servers, GPUI, Bevy, Ratatui/FrankenTUI, or application composition.
design: Keep the prototype disposable and outside tracked project source. Compare a synchronous/manual HostCore plus dedicated native driver with the minimal Asupersync two-phase bounded MPSC, cancellation/obligation, virtual-time, and blocking-bridge APIs. The synchronous FrankenSQLite Connection remains constructed, used, closed, and dropped on its owner thread; the spike may pass DTO batches and receipts but may not move the connection. Preserve a browser/manual driver that does not require Asupersync. Create a tracked runtime crate only if measured dependency-direction and multi-frontend reuse evidence clears the repository new-file/new-crate bar.
acceptance_criteria: The bead records an accept, reject, or partial verdict; exact immutable source/version; minimal APIs used; dependency and feature closure; clean/incremental compile impact; overflow/backpressure semantics; cancellation and shutdown obligations; panic/task-leak behavior; blocking-worker ownership; and native/WASM constraints. It proves the proposed Cargo dependency DAG has no runtime-to-storage/frontend/server edge and explains why a crate boundary is or is not needed. The disposable prototype lives outside tracked source and is not shipped. No Tokio/Axum stack is removed and simulation math is never decomposed into independently scheduled async tasks.
notes: Sibling evidence: asupersync main was refreshed to 90949d62ffd6221873a047ea14c7b6bb0060849f, but execution must still choose and pin an immutable revision. This decision bead precedes protocol placement; it does not authorize a broad runtime migration or new product dependency by itself.

title: Define host, client, snapshot, event, and command protocol
description: Define the renderer-neutral host protocol at the dependency boundary selected by .4.3: synchronous HostCore ports, HostClient, CommandEnvelope, snapshot subscription, event cursor, status lookup, and a null frontend. Give every envelope a stable CommandId and one host AdmissionSequence total order. Add ControlRevision as the optimistic-control token, while keeping ScientificRevision, ConfigRevision, SnapshotRevision, and EventSequence as distinct typed domains.
design: ControlRevision advances exactly once for each successfully applied mutating or playback envelope in the unified total order and is the expected-revision CAS token returned to control clients; ScientificRevision advances with scientific transitions, ConfigRevision with applied config, SnapshotRevision with publication, and EventSequence with journal order. Model receipts on two independent axes instead of a misleading linear enum. ApplicationState is Admitted, Applied with actual tick/revisions, Rejected, or Failed. JournalState is NotRequired, Pending, CommittedVolatile, Durable, or Failed. An applied command can therefore remain journal-pending, become volatile-only in memory mode, or become durable in file mode without overwriting the fact that application already occurred. Duplicate CommandId returns the existing status and never reapplies.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol tests cover total ordering, duplicate CommandId, concurrent retry, expected ControlRevision conflict, validation rejection, application failure, disconnect and later lookup, monotonic typed revisions, and every valid ApplicationState/JournalState combination. The null frontend can submit Pause/Resume/Speed/Step/config/shutdown, observe snapshots/events/status, and drive the synchronous host with manual time. The public runtime API and null frontend expose no mutable WorldState, world mutex, storage connection, or renderer/server type. This bead does not falsely claim that legacy GPUI, Bevy, or TUI imports are gone; those migrate in their dedicated adapter beads.
notes: ControlRevision is the one cross-transport optimistic token; scientific/config revisions remain observability domains rather than competing command order tokens. Journal durability semantics are completed by .4.10. The renderer import ban applies to the new runtime API and null frontend here, then becomes repository-wide only after the legacy frontend migrations.

title: Implement pure sole-owner HostCore state machine
description: Implement the synchronous sole-owner HostCore state machine with no thread spawning and no Arc<Mutex<WorldState>>. HostCore owns WorldState by value, applies the .4.4 protocol under injected/manual time, drives the pure transition from .4.2, retains journal work under backpressure, and publishes queryable health and two-axis command status. This is the sole authority for pause, speed, explicit Step, automatic stepping, command order, and scientific revisions.
design: Use one exact boundary algorithm: (1) observe lifecycle state and admit envelopes with stable AdmissionSequence; (2) at the next boundary deduplicate and validate expected ControlRevision; (3) apply envelopes strictly in sequence, advancing ControlRevision only on successful application; (4) execute each explicit Step exactly once at its ordered position, pausing before it and leaving paused unless a later envelope resumes, with no implicit cadence step in that boundary; (5) if no explicit Step consumed the boundary and final playback is Running, derive the bounded normal step budget from injected time/speed; (6) consume each StepOutcome, assign scientific/event revisions, and form the exact lossless journal batch; (7) try nonblocking journal admission, retaining the identical batch and latching a science-stop fault if full; (8) publish application status and latest state, while later worker acknowledgements advance only JournalState; (9) process ordered idempotent shutdown according to its admission position. Never reread mutable world to reconstruct a rejected batch.
acceptance_criteria: Manual-time tests prove initial paused/running states; Pause/Resume/Speed; Step while paused and running; Step-then-Resume gives one tick/final Running; Resume-then-Step gives one tick/final Paused; multiple Steps each advance once; no extra cadence tick shares a Step boundary; mixed command classes retain order; duplicate IDs do not reapply; conflicts do not advance ControlRevision; and 1/32/33/1000-envelope bursts have explicit outcomes. A full journal port retains byte-for-byte or value-equal completed work, prevents later science ticks, and admits the same batch on retry. HostCore contains no Arc<Mutex<WorldState>> and needs no renderer, server, database, or native scheduler. Production startup performs zero hidden warmup ticks; any requested warmup is an explicit manifest field/command with recorded tick/digest evidence, never an implicit 120-step loop.
notes: Use fake snapshot/journal/status ports for deterministic host-core tests; .4.10 supplies the production FrankenSQLite implementation later. The no-world-mutex claim applies to HostCore ownership and its new API, not to legacy frontends that have not yet migrated. Keep fixes discovered here focused; renderer and storage-worker defects get their owning beads.

title: Drive HostCore with fixed-deadline native lifecycle
description: Drive the exact .4.5 HostCore with a native fixed-deadline lifecycle. The driver owns scheduling, wakeups, cancellation, and bounded catch-up only; it cannot mutate WorldState except by invoking HostCore. Use the minimal Asupersync pieces selected by .4.3, or the documented alternative, while keeping manual/browser drivers independent.
design: Inject a monotonic clock and use deadline progression rather than repaint/frame deltas. Commands wake the driver, but only HostCore boundary processing changes control or science. Bound missed-deadline catch-up and record skipped wall-clock opportunity without inventing extra science order. Graceful Shutdown is an idempotent ordered envelope: define when new admissions close, finish or terminally reject earlier/pending envelopes in order, retain unadmitted journal work, request storage flush through the port, publish final status, and join every owned task before returning. Cancellation and panic paths satisfy explicit obligations and never bypass status bookkeeping silently.
acceptance_criteria: Manual and native drivers produce identical command, StepOutcome, ControlRevision, EventSequence, and WorldDigest traces for the same injected deadline/command schedule. Tests cover early/late/backward clock observations, wake storms, bounded catch-up, long pause with low CPU, cancellation before/during/after a step, queue-full science stop, shutdown with empty/nonempty queues, flush timeout/failure, and repeated idempotent shutdown. Repaint count and number of synthetic clients cannot affect ticks. The new production host lifecycle exposes no world lock and leaves no detached simulation/scheduler task. This bead does not claim the legacy Bevy driver or GPUI/TUI world access is gone before their adapter migrations.
notes: Native lifecycle only; browser/WASM may call the same HostCore from its own adapter but requestAnimationFrame must not become scientific time. Storage implementation and frontend teardown remain separate beads.

title: Publish immutable multi-subscriber snapshots
description: Publish immutable, renderer-neutral RenderSnapshot values from the sole-owner host: current tick/summary, run and control health, typed revisions, compact dynamic agents, and Arc-shared terrain/food/hydrology layers keyed by content revision. Provide bounded latest-value multi-subscriber semantics with an independent cursor for every consumer.
design: Snapshot publication is a lossy latest-value read model, not the scientific event journal and not a database query. Build snapshots only from HostCore-owned state/StepOutcome at the declared cadence; static layers reuse Arc values until their own revision changes, dynamic data uses a measured compact representation, and selected-agent detail is requested separately. Each subscriber may skip stale frames and load the newest Arc without retaining an unbounded queue. SnapshotRevision is publication order and never substitutes for ControlRevision, ScientificRevision, ConfigRevision, or EventSequence.
acceptance_criteria: Two fast subscribers plus stalled, dropped, and reconnecting subscribers remain independently bounded; the newest snapshot is coherent and monotonic; static layer pointer/content changes occur only with the matching revision; current summary advances independently of persistence cadence; and snapshot cadence/subscriber load cannot change WorldDigest or tick count. Measure allocation, bytes, build p50/p95, and 1k/10k agent costs. The new host/client API exposes no Arc<Mutex<WorldState>>, mutable core references, or FrankenSQLite handle. This does not falsely assert legacy frontends are migrated; .6.1 and .7.2 remove their old world-lock paths.
notes: Scientific events and gap recovery are implemented by .4.8. Frontend-specific camera, selection, top-K, glyph, and chart work must not become global mutable snapshot state.

title: Add per-client projections and sequenced event journal
description: Add deterministic renderer-neutral projections keyed by client/request and a bounded sequenced scientific-event journal. Viewport, camera, selection, requested detail, and chart windows are per-client inputs; no client can mutate global projection or scientific state. Event subscribers use EventSequence cursors, detect gaps, and either catch up from the journal or report an explicit truncated display window.
design: Projection functions are pure functions of immutable snapshot plus request and may use a keyed cache whose identity includes all request and source revisions. The hot event ring carries ordered notifications/cursors, while the journal is the lossless source. A cursor yields contiguous batches or an explicit Gap containing expected and available sequence ranges plus a catch-up locator. Events with JournalState Pending are never evicted or overwritten; reaching high water stops later science through HostCore until the exact batch is acknowledged. File-mode Durable records support crash-safe catch-up. CommittedVolatile memory-mode records may leave the hot ring only while the live in-memory journal remains queryable and must never be advertised as crash-durable.
acceptance_criteria: Two clients with different cameras, selections, detail requests, and chart windows produce isolated deterministic projections and cannot affect each other, world digests, or scientific revisions. Tests cover contiguous cursor reads, duplicate polling, slow consumers, ring wrap, explicit Gap metadata, durable file-journal catch-up, live memory-journal catch-up, unavailable catch-up, disconnect/reconnect, and shutdown. No Pending event is evicted; high-water pressure retains exact events and pauses before loss. Projection/event memory, latency, and top-K/canvas scaling are measured, and slow UI consumers never create an unbounded queue.
notes: This bead defines event sequencing and catch-up behavior; .4.10 implements production journal admission, acknowledgements, watermarks, and crash-durability proof. Presentation screens and renderer-specific picking remain in frontend beads.

title: Migrate CLI, REST, and MCP control to HostClient
description: Migrate the control CLI, REST, MCP, SSE, and NDJSON surfaces to the same HostClient/service contract. Remove their direct SharedWorld locks and projected-before-applied responses. Expose Pause, Resume, Step, Speed, status lookup, config/selection commands, and ordered graceful Shutdown with CommandId, expected ControlRevision, and the two-axis application/journal receipt. Add an explicit server-only application mode that runs the authoritative host with no visual frontend.
design: One transport-neutral control service performs validation, submits HostClient envelopes, reads immutable snapshots/status, and maps typed failures consistently; CLI, REST, and MCP are adapters only. Centralize the REST default at http://127.0.0.1:8088 so scriptbots-control, server configuration, help, README, and tests agree. SSE and NDJSON records carry monotonic sequence/revision fields, stable event IDs, heartbeat/schema metadata, bounded payloads, and explicit gap/reconnect behavior rather than polling a world lock. A state-changing request either waits to its documented application/journal level or returns Accepted with a status URL/ID; it never returns a fabricated future config as current.
acceptance_criteria: In explicit server mode with no renderer, CLI, REST, and MCP all perform Pause, Resume, Step, Speed, valid/invalid config, status lookup, and idempotent Shutdown with equivalent CommandId, ControlRevision, ApplicationState, JournalState, error, and retry semantics. scriptbots-control defaults to port 8088. A transport-conformance suite runs the same vectors for duplicate ID, stale revision, validation rejection, queue full, disconnected host, storage pending/failure, and shutdown pending across CLI/REST/MCP. SSE and NDJSON tests prove monotonic nonduplicated sequences, resume/gap behavior, response bounds, and cancellation cleanup. Reads use immutable snapshots; ASCII capture has real content/provenance, while unavailable live PNG capture returns a typed honest error rather than empty success.
notes: This bead migrates control transports, not TUI/GUI rendering internals. It must not claim crash durability beyond .4.10 acknowledgements, and it must not substitute a semantic CPU PNG for a live frontend framebuffer. Keep loopback defaults and schema/version discovery agent-friendly.

title: Replay, persistence, and experiment data
description: Implement run-scoped provenance, commands/events/checkpoints/digests, deterministic bundles, multi-run FrankenSQLite persistence, export, and verification.

title: Design multi-run FrankenSQLite schema and provenance migrations
description: Replace single-run primary-key assumptions with run-scoped FrankenSQLite tables for manifests, configs, seeds, features/build/source provenance, agents/lineages, metrics, commands, events, checkpoints, and digests. Use versioned transactional MigrationRunner/user_version migrations and validation.
design: Build on the proven fsqlite storage boundary and coordinate with bounded runtime storage while keeping schema logic independently testable. No destructive migration without explicit user permission; create/migrate test databases only. Plan sections 7.1 and 7.6.
acceptance_criteria: Two runs with overlapping ticks/agent ordinals coexist; run_id participates in all required keys; manifest provenance is queryable; migration is transactionally tested; schema version and failure recovery are explicit; analytics queries remain bounded.

title: Persist sequenced command status and domain event journals
description: Persist commands, tick-boundary status transitions, nonempty lifecycle/combat/domain events, event sequence, and digest references using the runtime durability protocol.
design: Uses corrected core accounting and runtime storage worker. Do not reconstruct events from aggregate metrics. Plan sections 7.2-7.4.
acceptance_criteria: Admitted/applied/durable/rejected/failed transitions are queryable; event sequences detect gaps/duplicates; births/deaths/combat between persistence intervals survive; an empty domain-event stream cannot satisfy a scenario expected to emit events.

title: Implement full checkpoints and first-divergence replay
description: Persist and restore world, brain genome/evaluator state, RNG streams, commands, config, environment, counters, and manifest; replay from tick zero or checkpoint and report the first stage/tick divergence.
design: Builds on digest/checkpoint envelope, runtime protocol, and journals. Do not call two empty vectors a successful replay. Plan Phase 4.1.
acceptance_criteria: Encode/decode is idempotent; next-tick output after restore matches; tick-zero and checkpoint replay match WorldDigestV1 in the bit-exact lane; empty evidence fails; divergence output identifies tick, stage, expected/actual digest, and relevant artifact.

title: Assemble and verify portable deterministic run bundles
description: Package manifest/source provenance, commands/status, events, checkpoints, digests, the FrankenSQLite run database, exports, and artifact index with integrity hashes and an import/verify command.
design: No silent best-effort verification. Packaging is separate from release distribution. Plan Phase 4.2.
acceptance_criteria: A second clean checkout using the pinned toolchain verifies a bundle; missing/tampered files fail with a precise reason; artifact paths are relative and portable; bundle schema is versioned; verification does not require GUI.

title: Build deterministic matched-seed experiment runner
description: Run scenario variants over matched seed cohorts with bounded concurrency, checkpoint/resume/branch, progress/status, and reproducible summaries using the canonical HostCore and bundle formats.
design: Scientific execution layer, not a UI. Depends on honest brain families, runtime, and bundle verification. Plan Phase 4.3.
acceptance_criteria: An MLP-versus-DWRAON sample produces comparable run bundles with identical environment seed schedule; interrupted batches resume without duplicate runs; concurrency does not change individual digests; resource bounds and failure policy are documented.
